description: IHData is the metocean data service of IHCantabria, the Environmental Hydraulics Institute of the University of Cantabria, which provides wind, wave and sea level climate statistics for research or commercial purposes. Its wave data come from hindcasts and projections generated by numerical models and include bulk sea-state parameters, sea and swell components and 3D wave spectra, with periods of more than 30 years. There are three products: GOW (Global Ocean Waves), a global WaveWatch III hindcast forced by atmospheric reanalyses with hourly parameters over more than 40 years and 5 to 25 km resolution, validated against deep-water buoys and altimetry; ROW (Regional Ocean Waves), SWAN-based regional datasets for zones with complex bathymetry or coastline; and DOW (Downscaling Ocean Waves), a hybrid dynamical and statistical downscaling of coastal waves at 1 km to 100 m for the Spanish, Brazilian and European coasts, validated against buoys. Data are supplied through a purchase procedure, and the team advises on the best product for each project; no open licence is stated. Caveats: the data are not openly downloadable, and custom datasets can be generated for a project area. Coverage is global, with high resolution for the Spanish, Brazilian and European coasts. It supports hazard exposure and design analysis for ports, coastal defences and offshore energy; related records are the Danish high water statistics and the CEREMA coastal erosion indicator.
